segments.title: 第72章 變態
segments.content:
Reigniting the Prime of Youth Chapter 72: Pervert

In Yuhang City, September was still as hot as summer, even though it was technically autumn.

On Houde Road, most of the students heading to the cafeteria were still just wearing their short-sleeved school uniforms.

The youthful faces reflected in Li Luo's eyes, letting him truly feel a vibrant energy he hadn't experienced in a long time.

If he were walking with three beautiful girls he didn't know, even with the soul of a 35-year-old, Li Luo estimated he would still feel a bit awkward.

But with Ying Chanxi, Yan Zhusheng, and Xu Youyu, whom he had known in his past life, he felt quite at ease.

Fuyi High School was completely unfamiliar to Li Luo.

He had never been here in his previous life.

He knew nothing about this prestigious institution.

He had only caught a glimpse of the tip of the iceberg from occasional chats with Zhao Rongjun.

Now that he was immersed in it, he naturally saw a side completely different from what he had once imagined.

For instance, the club activities.

In his memory, his high school in his past life definitely didn't have such things.

But at Fuyi High, although the main clubs were competition-oriented, many students with strengths in certain subjects would try to sign up for a subject-based club to see if they could try their hand at academic competitions.

Yet, aside from those few competition clubs, there were indeed many interest-driven clubs.

This was something completely unimaginable in Li Luo's previous understanding.

As he saw it, the academic pressure in his high school back then was already immense, with teachers constantly hyping up the students to put them under high pressure, often saying things like "if you don't get into a good university, you'll end up screwing bolts in a factory."

So, as the top contender in Yinjiang District, the academic pressure at Fuyi High must be astronomical.

Thus, Li Luo could comfort himself with the thought that perhaps not getting into Fuyi High wasn't such a bad thing; at least his high school life wouldn't be under even greater pressure.

But now that he had truly experienced campus life at Fuyi High, Li Luo suddenly realized something.

Schools with truly high teaching standards might not all be products of high-pressure environments.

"Senior," Li Luo said, turning his head curiously while walking toward the cafeteria, "I feel like our school isn't that strict. There are a lot of clubs, and the curriculum doesn't seem too packed. Won't this affect academic performance?"

Xu Youyu didn't expect Li Luo to suddenly ask such a question. She paused for a moment, then said, "It's probably the atmosphere."

"The students at Fuyi High are the best from Yinjiang District. We all fundamentally understand the importance of studying."

"If you see everyone around you studying hard, you'll naturally feel a sense of urgency and subconsciously join in with the atmosphere to study."

"Besides, what's wrong with having a rich variety of club activities?"

"According to our principal, participating more in sports and trying out more hobbies enriches both the body and mind, which in turn makes studying twice as effective."

Fuyi High's Principal Wang was a retired military man, so it wasn't strange that he held such views, given his deeply ingrained military spirit.

The group went to the cafeteria for lunch.

Because of the Student Council, Xu Youyu had to continue patrolling the area afterward, so she ate rather quickly.

But she didn't forget to say, "Once you guys join the Student Council, I can finally relax. I'll just order you all around then."

"I'm not joining," Li Luo said, shaking his head repeatedly.

He remembered clearly that when he joined the student council in vocational college in his past life, it was full of all sorts of ridiculous nonsense.

But Xu Youyu looked at him strangely and reminded him, "Our school calls it the Student Council, but it's not quite the same as a university's student council. It's actually just made up of the class presidents and Youth League secretaries from each class. So, since you're the class president, you've automatically joined."

"???" Li Luo was dumbfounded, but then he remembered Saturday's class committee election and immediately felt relieved. "Well, that's fine. It's not like I planned on staying as president anyway."

"You're not going to be class president anymore?" Ying Chanxi frowned. "You worked so hard to get the position, why resign?"

"Being class president is so tiring. I prefer to take it easy."

In any case, Li Luo had made up his mind not to run for class president. Whoever wanted the job could have it.

After a quick lunch, Xu Youyu was the first to leave.

Li Luo waited for Ying Chanxi and the others to finish their meals at a leisurely pace before the group went for a stroll along Houde Road.

Yan Zhusheng went to the Rock Music Club, and after casually showing off her skills, she passed the interview smoothly.

With nothing better to do, Li Luo also went and played the guitar for a bit, but he hadn't decided whether to join, so he politely declined the Rock Music Club's invitation.

Afterward, he accompanied Ying Chanxi to check out the Literature Club, where they ran into Hua Xiuxiu and Lin Yuan, who were also there.

"Didn't you say you weren't coming?" Hua Xiuxiu asked strangely upon seeing Li Luo. "Changed your mind and want to join?"

"She wanted to come, I'm just here with her," Li Luo said, pointing at Ying Chanxi, then glanced at the Literature Club's entry requirements.

Besides those who had won awards or scored full marks on the high school entrance exam essay, all other students needed to pass a simple test to officially join.

The test was indeed simple, just some multiple-choice questions about famous literary works, like whether *Dawn Blossoms Plucked at Dusk* was a collection of prose or something else.

Since Ying Chanxi hadn't participated in any Chinese essay competitions in junior high and hadn't taken the high school entrance exam, she had to take the test.

But for her, it wasn't difficult at all.

After they were done with the Literature Club, Li Luo accompanied her to look at a few other competition clubs.

In the end, Ying Chanxi chose the Math Club, fulfilling the expectations of their homeroom teacher, Teacher Sun.

After looking around, Li Luo eventually wandered over to the Basketball Club and joined up with Zhu Yufei and the others, deciding to follow Principal Wang's advice to participate more in sports and get some exercise.

But just as today's club recruitment was winding down and the evening self-study session began, someone suddenly came to the door looking for Li Luo at the end of the first period.

"Li Luo, someone's here for you," Hua Xiuxiu, who sat near the door, called out to Li Luo. "It's the vice president of the Literature Club."

Li Luo, sitting in the corner by the window, stood up and walked to the front door of the classroom, where he saw Qin Yawei, who introduced herself as the vice president.

"Hello, Li Luo," Qin Yawei said with a smile, introducing herself. "I'm Qin Yawei, the vice president of the Literature Club. It's a pleasure to meet you."

"Um..." Li Luo was in the middle of his homework, hoping to finish it in the first two self-study periods so he wouldn't have to do it at home and could start writing his novel. "If this is about joining the club, I'll have to refuse. I'm sorry."

"Huh?" Qin Yawei hadn't expected him to refuse so decisively before she had even said anything. Her expression changed instantly. "Why not join? Other than you, everyone in our school who got a full score on the entrance exam essay has already joined the Literature Club."

"Then you're not short one person, are you?" Li Luo asked with a strange look. "In any case, thank you for the offer, but I'll be heading back now."

"Hey, wait!" Qin Yawei quickly grabbed his arm. "The Literature Club is really relaxed. You just need to submit one manuscript a month, and there are almost no other requirements. The weekly Pen Pal Club meetings are voluntary too. If you've joined another club, it won't be a problem to join the Literature Club as well."

Normally, even for a student who got full marks on the entrance exam essay, Qin Yawei wouldn't be this persistent.

It was purely because after the National Day holiday, the Literature Club would hold a new election for its president.

According to the rules, third-year students had to withdraw from all clubs to focus on their final year of preparation for the college entrance exams.

The club presidents, however, would remain until around the National Day holiday of their first semester, handing over their duties and selecting a new president before completely withdrawing.

And Qin Yawei's current competitor was Xu Youyu.

Although this was just a small recruitment drive, it was still a task.

Qin Yawei knew she wasn't as good-looking as Xu Youyu, and the boys in the club favored Xu Youyu. So, she could only work harder on small things like this to gain a competitive edge.

But she never would have thought that this guy, Li Luo, would be so uncooperative.

Would it kill you to join?

But Li Luo was also a bit speechless, thinking, *Will I die if I don't join the Literature Club?*

He pulled his arm out of Qin Yawei's grasp and sighed. "Senior Qin, I'm really not interested in the Literature Club. You should stop wasting your time on me."

Just then, the bell rang, signaling the start of the second evening self-study period.

Li Luo waved and returned to his seat. At the doorway, Qin Yawei's expression flickered between anger and disappointment. Finally, she could only stomp her foot and return to her own classroom.

At 8:30 PM, after the second evening self-study period ended, Ying Chanxi came to find Li Luo to go home.

"Aren't we waiting for our senior to go back with us?" Li Luo asked as they went downstairs.

"I asked her earlier. She said she has to deal with the Literature Club's recruitment matters after class and needs to attend a meeting. But she reminded you to make a late-night snack when you get home. She wants fried noodles." As Ying Chanxi spoke, she added, "Me too."

"...You two really aren't afraid of getting fat."

"I'm very slim, okay? You should say that to our senior instead."

"Mmm... you're right."

"Where are your eyes wandering?! Pervert!"

(End of Chapter)
